summary: Maine's original Trout Mountain fire tower (on a Forest Service map by 1931, closed in the 1970s) is in ruins; an 80-ft tower rebuilt from Alabama parts went up on the summit in 2020.

facts.status_note: The original Maine tower lies in ruins on the ground. A separate 80-ft tower, rebuilt in 2020 from salvaged and new steel, stands on the summit.
facts.design: 80-ft steel observation tower built in 2020 from the middle sections of a 120-ft Alabama tower plus newly galvanized steel
facts.agency: The Nature Conservancy, Maine chapter (Trout Mountain Preserve)

notes_for_editor: Covers the original Maine tower only. The 2020 standing tower already has its own record and story (us-me-trout-mountain), and the FFLA list shows it as a separate entry at 45.80238 -68.85003 (us-me-trout-mountain-2 original at 45.80191 -68.84884). Consider linking or merging the two. The brief's status 'gone' is right for the original. The 1931 move rests on two sources (Maine Memory caption beside a Black Cat photo, and the Former Fire Lookout Sites record for Black Cat); neither gives a build date for the Trout Mountain tower, so no build event is dated. The sources give the closure only as 'the 1970s', so no closure event is dated. Elevation disagrees (1,409 / 1,408 / 1,427 ft). Facebook posts from the FFLA Maine chapter could not be read and are not cited.
